headline: Jarry’s shutout against Flames a hopeful sign of things to come
take:
Daily Faceoff's Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton called Jarry's shutout against the Flames a hopeful sign for the Oilers, and said Edmonton needs that kind of goaltending right now.

Our numbers explain the urgency. EDM is 9-2-2, but goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie or team stops compared with what the quality of shots against would predict, sits at minus 6.4 so far this season. That means the Oilers have given up about six more goals than the chances warranted. The record has been carried by scoring: EDM has put in 15.2 more goals than its chances would predict, and its share of expected goals, the quality of chances taken versus allowed, is only 52.8 percent overall and 49 percent at five-on-five. A team living on finishing luck with shaky goaltending is fragile, so one shutout matters less than whether the saves keep coming.

CGY's side shows how close the margin is. The Flames are 5-7-0 with a 46.7 percent expected goals share and are 6.6 goals short of expectation at scoring, so their results trail their play slightly. Edmonton would benefit most if Jarry steadies the minus 6.4.
